key_insight: A Krotov-inspired hybrid optimizer transfers optimal-control updates to quantum circuits, with a batch direction equal to the exact empirical-loss gradient for fixed-generator gates and terminal-state losses.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a first-order-cost training alternative for variational quantum classifiers, with batch-phase descent and convergence guarantees under standard smoothness assumptions.
method: Replace time-local control updates with gate-index-local circuit updates.
Use forward-state propagation, costate propagation, and local parameter updates.
Switch from online updates to batch optimization after a finite initial phase.
evidence_signal: Matched hyperparameter sweeps with three seeds per configuration on four-bit parity and the Pérez-Salinas crown classifier showed stronger performance than tuned first-order PennyLane baselines on parity and accuracy approaching L-BFGS-B on the crown task.
watch_item: The guarantees depend on the specified gate/loss structure and smoothness assumptions; the two small classification benchmarks do not establish large-scale or hardware performance.
paper_title: Hybrid Krotov gradient descent Optimization for Quantum Machine Learning
